transcript:
User: We have a girl at the front desk, she picks up fine. Not sure why I'd need this.
Agent: Got it, if she’s handling things well it makes sense you’d question adding anything else.  

Mhm, when she’s at lunch, out sick, or if two calls come in at once, what usually happens to those extra calls?
User: We just call people back when we can. Never really counted how many we miss.
Agent: Yeah, that’s super common — most places just return calls when they get a minute.  

When you do call back, do people usually still book with you, or do you feel like some of those have already moved on by then?
User: Most of the time they book, but I'm sure a few have moved on. Never really tracked it closely.
Agent: Makes sense, if most still book it doesn’t feel like a fire to put out.  

So if I could help you see exactly how many calls you’re actually missing and what that’s worth in lost revenue each month, would that even be interesting to you, or not really a priority right now?
User: Sounds like a solution looking for a problem. Janet's been here 9 years; she's got it covered.
Agent: Totally hear you — if Janet’s rock solid and has been with you 9 years, that’s a big asset.  

Out of curiosity, when Janet’s off for the day or on vacation, what usually happens with the phones then?
User: We manage. Sometimes I or someone else will cover, but it's not a big issue for us.
Agent: Gotcha, so from your side it feels pretty under control and not really a headache.  

If nothing changed with your phones for the next 2–3 years, would you be totally fine with that, or are there any goals where you’d *like* more calls or new clients coming in?
User: We're doing okay as is. More calls are nice, but not really a pressing goal right now.
Agent: Totally hear you — if things are working and growth isn’t urgent, you don’t need another project on your plate.  

So if I *didn’t* try to sell you anything and just asked: if your call volume suddenly doubled next month, could your team handle it the same way you do now, or would something start to strain?
User: If call volume doubled, we'd definitely feel the strain. Backup could be useful in that scenario.
Agent: That makes a lot of sense — so right now you’re fine, but if things jump, you’d want backup so Janet’s not drowning.  

When you picture that “doubled calls” world, what would you want covered first: new callers trying to book, existing clients with quick questions, or after‑hours calls?
User: Probably new callers trying to book. If we miss them, we're potentially losing new business right off the bat.
Agent: Yeah, that’s exactly where this matters — first‑time callers are the easiest to lose and the hardest to get back.  

So right now, if a brand‑new caller doesn’t get picked up and never calls back, what do you think that lost customer is worth to you over a year?
User: We'd probably lose about $1,100 per missed call that doesn't get returned. It's not ideal, but manageable.
Agent: Got it, so roughly eleven hundred bucks walking out the door each time a new caller slips through and never comes back is “not ideal but manageable” right now.  

If we could step in only when Janet can’t grab the phone—so every new caller either books or at least leaves with a confirmed next step—would you be open to seeing how that might work for your office, or would you rather leave it for now?
User: Alright, as a backup layer I can see it. Book your demo. What's the next step?
Agent: Love it, that makes sense as a backup layer.  

Do you prefer a quick 20‑minute Zoom with Jay in the next few days, or would next week be better for you?
User: Next week works. Let’s set up a time then. Can you text me the details?
Agent: Got it, next week works.  

What day next week is best for you for about 20 minutes with Jay – early in the week or later toward Thursday/Friday?
User: Let's go with Thursday morning. Can you send me the details by text? Looking forward to it.
Agent: Perfect, Thursday morning it is.  

Last thing—what’s your first name so I can lock this in properly for Jay?
User: Just put it under Dave. I'll look out for the details. Thanks.
Agent: Thanks, Dave — I’ll get you set for Thursday morning with Jay and we’ll text you the details so you’ve got the link and time handy. If anything comes up, you can just reply to that text to adjust; otherwise, talk to you Thursday and have a great rest of your day.
